spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A generalized coefficient in the symmetric phase combination is constrained by simultaneous real and imaginary cancellation, making the equal-weight choice structurally special within the stated family.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For B=exp(i theta)+b exp(-i theta-prime), the endnote sets real and imaginary parts to zero, combines the equations to obtain cos(theta+theta-prime)=-(b+1/b)/2, and concludes that only b=1 admits solutions under its coefficient assumptions.
directed.conceptual_reading: Compatibility of two real constraints can eliminate apparently free representation choices and single out the symmetric normalization.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Separating B=0 into real and imaginary equations bridges complex cancellation to a scalar feasibility bound.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is a local algebraic constraint on one coefficient family, not evidence that the chosen phase branch captures all zeta zeros; the stated inequality also depends on an unstated domain for b in this narrow span.
directed.uncertainty: Primes, inequalities, and coefficient notation are extraction-damaged, so the exact derivation and assumptions on b require PDF verification.

supported: The endnote explicitly separates B=0 into real and imaginary equations and reports cos(theta+theta-prime)=-(b+1/b)/2.
The candidate correctly says this local coefficient calculation does not establish completeness of the chosen phase branch.
It notices that the conclusion depends on an unstated domain for b.
inference: A feasibility bound can constrain coefficient choices once a domain such as positive real b is supplied.
